notes: Four BiLSTM arms on the current canonical split (TODO §3.6). bilstm_base: the exact, unmodified sb.recognize.architectures.BiLSTM class fed base_v1 ME-126/xy raw landmarks (252-dim) -- a faithful re-baseline, since every registry BiLSTM run predates the 2026-09-16 split reset, so it keeps `shared`'s batch_size/lr exactly as gislr.training.json has them (no override) for a true replica. bilstm_curated: the new LandmarkBiLSTM (attention gate + learned 922->256 projection bottleneck before the LSTM, generalized dims every other interp-track model has) fed features_curated's ME-126+xy+28-angle+relational pipeline (922-dim), batch_size overridden higher to use the GPU's headroom -- no historical regime to stay faithful to. CAUTION (2026-09-19): an earlier version of this config also 4x'd `lr` (linear batch-size scaling) alongside the 4x batch_size bump -- that combination collapsed bilstm_curated into a uniform predictor from epoch 1 (loss pinned at ln(250)=5.52, val_acc stuck at chance 0.4%, early-stopped at epoch 16). Adam-family optimizers don't tolerate that scaling rule without a warmup; verified on real data that dropping the lr override (keeping production's 0.001414 at batch 4096) breaks the collapse. Do not re-add an lr override here without a warmup schedule and a repeated real-data check like the one that caught this. RE-RUN 2026-09-2x (after the lr fix): the collapse is gone, but bilstm_curated still loses to bilstm_base by ~16pp top-1 (0.578 vs 0.737) and overfits MORE (val_acc peaks epoch 80/96 then drifts down, val_loss rising from epoch ~48 while train_loss keeps falling) despite having 3.6x the raw feature dimensionality. Two confounded changes vs bilstm_base: the attention+projection architecture, and the 4x batch size. **bilstm_curated_plainarch** and **bilstm_curated_b1024** (added 2026-09-2x, TODO §3.6 ablation) isolate them: plainarch feeds the same 922-dim curated features straight into the unmodified BiLSTM class (no attention gate, no projection, no batch change) to test whether the feature set alone explains the gap; b1024 keeps LandmarkBiLSTM's attention+projection but drops back to shared's batch_size=1024 to test whether batch size alone explains it. Not part of ARCHS/the registry -- see sb.recognize.interp's module docstring for why. All four arms are OFFLINE-ONLY (bidirectional).

bilstm_base.description: sb.recognize.architectures.BiLSTM, unmodified, fed base_v1 ME_126/xy (252-dim). No overrides -- exact replica of the production regime.

bilstm_curated.description: sb.recognize.interp.models.LandmarkBiLSTM, fed features_curated (922-dim). batch_size overridden (below) to use the GPU's headroom -- no historical regime to stay faithful to. lr is deliberately NOT overridden -- see the top-level `notes` for why.

bilstm_curated_plainarch.description: ABLATION arm 1/2 (isolates the feature set): the unmodified sb.recognize.architectures.BiLSTM class (same as bilstm_base, no attention gate, no projection bottleneck) fed features_curated (922-dim) directly as input_size. batch_size NOT overridden (shared's 1024, matching bilstm_base) -- the only variable vs bilstm_base is the feature set itself.

bilstm_curated_b1024.description: ABLATION arm 2/2 (isolates batch size): LandmarkBiLSTM, same attention gate + projection as bilstm_curated, fed features_curated (922-dim). batch_size NOT overridden (shared's 1024) -- the only variable vs bilstm_curated is batch size.
